legal_004:n1.prompt:
You are helping me draft a standard SaaS subscription agreement, terms of service, and privacy policy using {{vendor}}, our AI assistant tool. 

First, ask me for any of the following details you don't already have: our company's legal name, the SaaS product name, governing law/jurisdiction, subscription pricing/billing model (e.g., monthly/annual, per-seat), trial period length, data types we collect from customers/users, whether we use subprocessors or third-party analytics tools, support/SLA commitments, and termination/renewal terms.

Once you have these inputs, use {{vendor}} to: (1) draft a SaaS subscription agreement covering license grant, fees, payment terms, term/termination, warranties, limitation of liability, and confidentiality; (2) draft a terms of service document covering acceptable use, account responsibilities, and dispute resolution; (3) draft a privacy policy covering data collection, use, storage, sharing, and user rights consistent with common frameworks (e.g., GDPR/CCPA style language) adapted to the details I gave you. Iterate on each document within {{vendor}} until the structure, clauses, and placeholders (e.g., [Company Name], [Effective Date]) are clean and consistent across all three documents, then export each as a separate file (e.g., Word or PDF).

Done looks like: three complete, internally consistent draft documents, clearly labeled, with all placeholders filled in from my inputs and any remaining open questions (e.g., unresolved legal terms) flagged in a short notes section.

Because a human must explicitly approve before these drafts are applied or sent externally, do not finalize, send, or treat these as binding — present the exported drafts and a summary of key terms/assumptions, then stop for human sign-off.

legal_004:n2.prompt:
You are helping me draft a Terms of Service (ToS) document as part of finalizing our SaaS agreement package (alongside a subscription agreement and privacy policy). Use our configured {{vendor}} AI assistant to create and iteratively edit this document.

Before starting, ask me for any of the following if not already provided: our company/legal entity name, product or service name, company address/jurisdiction, governing law preference, support contact/email, and any known business specifics (e.g., subscription billing model, free trial terms, acceptable use restrictions, termination conditions, liability limitations) that should shape the ToS.

Actions to take:
1. Using {{vendor}}, draft a standard SaaS Terms of Service covering: acceptance of terms, description of service, account registration, subscription/payment terms, acceptable use policy, intellectual property rights, confidentiality, disclaimers/warranties, limitation of liability, indemnification, term and termination, governing law/dispute resolution, and modifications to terms.
2. Iterate on the draft within {{vendor}} to incorporate the specifics I provide, ensuring clarity and internal consistency with any subscription agreement or privacy policy language I share.
3. Export the finished draft as a clean, well-formatted document (e.g., Word or PDF) suitable for legal review.

Done looks like: a complete, exportable ToS draft that reflects our inputs, is internally consistent, and is ready for legal/compliance review — but not yet finalized or published.

Since approval is required before changes are applied, do not publish, send, or treat this draft as final. Prepare the draft, a summary of key clauses and any assumptions made, and a checklist of open questions needing my input, then stop for human sign-off.

Report back with the exported draft, your summary, and the checklist.

legal_004:n3.prompt:
You are helping me draft a Privacy Policy for our SaaS product using {{vendor}}, our AI assistant. Goal: produce a clear, legally-sound draft Privacy Policy document ready for human legal review and sign-off — you will not publish, apply, or finalize it.

First, ask me for any of these inputs you don't already have: company legal name, product/domain name, jurisdictions we operate in or target (e.g., US, EU/GDPR, CCPA), categories of personal data we collect (account info, usage data, payment data, cookies/analytics), any third-party subprocessors or tools we use (analytics, payment processor, hosting, email), data retention practices, whether we use cookies/tracking, and a contact email for privacy inquiries.

Then, using {{vendor}}, create a draft Privacy Policy document covering: what data is collected and how, purposes of processing, legal bases (if applicable), data sharing/subprocessors, data retention, user rights (access, deletion, opt-out, portability as relevant to named jurisdictions), cookie/tracking disclosures, security measures at a high level, children's privacy statement, policy update process, and contact information. Iterate on the draft within {{vendor}} until it is clear, internally consistent, and tailored to the inputs I provided. Export the final draft as a document file (e.g., Word or PDF) I can share with counsel.

Do not treat this draft as final, publish it, or embed it into our site or product. Do not attempt to sign, approve, or submit it anywhere. Prepare the exported draft, a short summary of key clauses and any open questions/assumptions you made, and then stop for human sign-off.

Report back with: the exported file/location, a bullet summary of key sections and any assumptions or missing inputs you had to guess, and a clear note that this requires legal review and explicit human approval before use.

legal_004:n4.prompt:
You are helping me prepare for legal counsel review of our SaaS subscription agreement, terms of service, and privacy policy (step legal_004:n4). This is a policy-gate step: you must prepare everything but a human (our legal counsel) must explicitly approve before any changes are applied — you may not approve, sign, or submit anything on my behalf.

First, ask me for anything missing: our company/domain name, the current drafts (or their file locations) of the SaaS agreement, ToS, and privacy policy, the name/contact of the reviewing counsel, and any known deadline.

Then do the following:
1. Consolidate the three documents into a single review package with version labels and dates.
2. Draft a cover memo summarizing: purpose of each document, key commercial terms (pricing, term length, liability caps, termination), and any open questions or risk areas you notice (e.g., unclear data processing terms, missing indemnification language).
3. Prepare a checklist of specific items for counsel to confirm or flag (e.g., liability limitation adequacy, compliance with applicable privacy law, dispute resolution clause).
4. Draft an email to the reviewing counsel attaching/linking the package, requesting their review and explicit sign-off, with a suggested response deadline.
5. Set up a way to track the review status (e.g., a shared doc or tracker entry marked 'pending counsel review').

Do not send the email or make any changes to the documents based on assumed approval. Once your package and email draft are ready, stop for human sign-off — present the draft materials to me for review and confirm counsel has been asked to approve. When counsel's decision arrives, note that this is an async step: I will need to poll/check back with counsel for their response, and you should ask me to confirm the outcome (approved / changes requested) before any next step proceeds. Report back with the package summary, draft email, checklist, and current review status.

legal_004:n5.prompt:
You are helping me prepare to publish our attorney-approved SaaS Subscription Agreement, Terms of Service, and Privacy Policy to our live website. Do NOT publish or make anything live — this step requires my explicit sign-off before changes go live.

First, ask me for anything you need that isn't already available: (1) the final approved text/documents for each of the three policies, (2) my website domain and which CMS or website platform we use (e.g., WordPress, Webflow, Squarespace, custom site) and confirmation I have configured credentials for it, (3) the target URLs/page slugs where each document should live (e.g., /terms, /privacy, /subscription-agreement), and (4) any footer/nav links that need to point to these pages.

Once you have the inputs, do the following: (a) prepare the exact page content for each of the three documents, formatted for the target CMS (headings, paragraphs, links) without altering the approved legal wording; (b) stage these as draft/unpublished pages in the CMS using my configured credentials, at the specified URLs; (c) prepare a side-by-side comparison checklist showing the staged draft text against the attorney-approved source text for each document, flagging any formatting differences (e.g., missing sections, truncated text, broken links); (d) draft the internal navigation/footer link updates as a proposed change list, but do not apply them live.

When finished, report back with: the staged draft URLs (or draft/preview links) for all three documents, the comparison checklist confirming text matches the approved source, and a summary of any discrepancies found. Then stop for human sign-off — I will personally verify the staged content against counsel's approved version and give the go-ahead before you publish anything live.
